stop_condition: Each of round 2's seven findings is verified fixed against the code and the F4 validation stores rather than against the author's description of the fix; the v5.0.0 ledger tally is re-run with the ledger's own five commands; and no fix introduced a new inaccuracy or left a corrected claim contradicted by prose on a sibling surface. No critical/high finding remains in the release-surface claims (CHANGELOG, README) or the v5.0.0 ledger rows.

findings.evidence: R2-F1's disproved claim is alive, word for word, in text ADDED BY THIS CHANGE SET. The residual bullet's bolded head reads: '**`design-conform` returns `ok:true` over an empty change set on a real target, and the coherence rollup inherits it (`DP4`, PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT as of 2026-09-30).**' `git diff -U0 docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md` shows the hunk `@@ -980,0 +985,14 @@` -- lines 985-998 are all new, so this is not stale leftover text but a fresh authoring of the claim round 2 blocked on. CHANGELOG.md:35, in the same change set, now says the opposite in terms: 'the rollup does not inherit the conformance check's answer, it repeats its mistake.' `grep -rn inherit README.md CHANGELOG.md docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md` returns exactly these two as live claims about the rollup, and they contradict. The code is unchanged from what round 2 established, re-verified at ecab070d: the LEG 1 guard is `if [ "$mode" != "rollup" ]; then` at qa-gate.sh:15182; compute_design_coherence's only alignment call is `compute_design_alignment "$mapped_task" "rollup"` at :15963; and `awk 'NR>=15663 && NR<=16294 { line=$0; sub(/^[ \t]+/,"",line); if (line !~ /^#/ && $0 ~ /design-conform/) print NR }' .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh` returns NOTHING -- zero non-comment references to design-conform anywhere in compute_design_coherence's body.
findings.description: The fix was applied to two of the three surfaces that carry the claim and not to the third -- the same half-fix shape as R2-F2 (CHANGELOG corrected, README left publishing the retracted numbers), repeating one round later on a different pair. It is worse here in one respect: the surviving copy is on the LEDGER, which is the evidence-of-record the release text points at, so a reader who follows the CHANGELOG's mechanism statement to its backing row finds the row asserting the mechanism the CHANGELOG just denied. It is also the bolded HEAD of the bullet, not a clause buried in it. Fix: restate :985-986 the way CHANGELOG.md:34-43 now does -- the rollup reaches the same vacuity INDEPENDENTLY, by its own `impact-report.sh --relativized-changed-files` read at qa-gate.sh:16119, with LEG 1 deliberately skipped for the correctness reason the function header at :15119-15144 states. Then re-run the `grep -rn inherit` sweep above and confirm the only surviving hits are the CHANGELOG's correct one and the three unrelated rows (UW16, DP5, DP17/DP18, :1178).

findings.evidence: The R2-F3 fix anchored the design-arc figure with a label that does not produce it. Both surfaces now say 3h23m43s is measured 'design task created -> last implementation completion' (CHANGELOG.md:66-69 '(design task created→last implementation completion): **3h23m43s** (`target-23z` created 2026-09-28 16:03:55Z→`target-23z.1` COMPLETION 19:27:38Z)'; README.md:227-228 '**3h23m43s** from design task created to last implementation completion'). Queried from the F4 clone's own flagship store at /var/folders/qr/c0gwdny174v7dbphnj1l7wy40000gn/T/cwpf4.XXXXXX.1Eqtm8TbLC/flagship via `bd show target-23z.1 --json --include-comments`, target-23z.1 carries THREE `COMPLETION v1 ... role=backend` records: 2026-09-28T18:53:07Z, 2026-09-28T19:27:38Z, and 2026-09-29T15:49:44Z. The LAST implementation completion is 2026-09-29T15:49:44Z. Against `target-23z` created 2026-09-28T16:03:55Z (confirmed by `bd show target-23z --json` -> created_at 2026-09-28T16:03:55Z) the stated anchor yields 23h45m49s, not 3h23m43s. The number itself is correct for a DIFFERENT anchor -- last SAME-DAY completion, 19:27:38Z, which is exactly the qualifier round 2's own evidence used ('last same-day COMPLETION v1') and exactly the word the fix dropped. The arithmetic of both figures checks out at their true anchors: 16:03:55Z->19:27:38Z = 3h23m43s, and 15:41:15Z->15:53:25Z = 12m10s.
findings.description: This is the R2-F3 defect re-introduced in a harder form: before, the figure had NO anchor and a reader could not re-derive it; now it has a CONFIDENT anchor that re-derives to a different number, seven times larger. It sits in the sentence both surfaces use to tell the reader which number to budget against ('The second number is the one to budget against'; 'The cost you are actually opting into'), and CONTRIBUTING.md's rule -- cited in this same CHANGELOG entry's own retraction note -- is that a number carries the command that produced it. A second claim falls with it: README.md:226-227 says the arc 'precedes' the gate cycle, which is true only under the same-day anchor (19:27:38Z precedes gate-enter at 15:41:15Z on 09-29) and FALSE under the stated one (15:49:44Z is after gate-enter). Fix: name the anchor that was actually measured on both surfaces -- 'design task created to the last SAME-DAY implementation completion', or equivalently 'to the last implementation completion BEFORE gate-enter' -- and keep 3h23m43s. Do not re-anchor to 23h45m49s: that interval contains the 20-hour overnight gap and would misdescribe the cost in the other direction.

findings.evidence: R2-F6 asked for the nouns to be made explicit 'in BOTH places'. The two release surfaces were changed to 'twice'; the ledger was not, and the ledger's own 'once' text was AUTHORED IN THIS CHANGE SET. Live now: CHANGELOG.md:43-44 '`design-conform` has been observed on a real repository exactly **twice**, and BOTH observations were VACUOUS'; README.md:209-210 'observed on a real target project exactly twice, and both observations were vacuous'. Against three ledger statements: (1) DP4's own bolded headline at :810, 'ITS RESULT IN A TARGET PROJECT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND THE ONE REAL-PROJECT OBSERVATION OF IT WAS VACUOUS' -- which its OWN body contradicts four sentences later with 'That happened twice, by two independent routes'; (2) the tally note at :852-854, '`DP4` was scoped to F4's evidence, PROVEN -> PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT, because the one real-project observation of `design-conform` was VACUOUS', which `git diff -U0` shows as a `+` line (hunk `@@ -851 +852,4 @@`) -- new text this cycle; (3) the residual bullet at :989-991, 'Observed exactly once on a real product repository, and that observation was vacuous ... Two independent routes reached it', also new this cycle (hunk `@@ -980,0 +985,14 @@`), self-contradictory in three lines. `grep -rn 'exactly once|one real-project|ONE REAL-PROJECT' README.md CHANGELOG.md docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md` returns these ledger hits and no release-surface hit. TWICE is the supported count: `bd show claude-workflow-plugin-pqoj` -> 'FOUND IN F4, the real-project validation run, 2026-09-29'; `bd show claude-workflow-plugin-q5l6` -> 'FOUND in the F4 flagship run on a real target, 2026-09-29, on a denylist-clean path -- so this is NOT claude-workflow-plugin-pqoj', and its measured trace lists `design-conform -> ok:true, "3 declared file(s) not yet touched", naming exactly the three files that WERE written and tested`. Both observations are of design-conform, both in the F4 run against a real target.
findings.description: The release surfaces are now RIGHT and the evidence row that backs them is WRONG, which is the worse direction: DP4 is where a reader goes to check the CHANGELOG's headline caveat, and it understates the evidence by half while contradicting itself inside one cell. The count is load-bearing -- it is the whole argument for shipping the design phase opt-in, and 'twice, by two independent routes' is a materially stronger case than 'once'. Note this is also the third consecutive round in which a correction landed on some surfaces and not all of them (R1-F5: CHANGELOG yes / README no; R2-F1: CHANGELOG yes / ledger no, see R3-F1; here: both release surfaces yes / ledger no). Fix all three ledger statements to the same noun-explicit form the release text now uses -- two observations of `design-conform` on a real target, both vacuous, reached by two independent routes -- and, while :810 is open, delete the 'THE ONE REAL-PROJECT OBSERVATION' clause rather than editing around it, since its own body already states the correct count.

findings.evidence: The new section's central table overclaims the refusal's reach. Row 1: '**None** of the declared files in the bound change set | **refuses**, `error_key=completion_files_total_miss`'. The refusal at qa-gate.sh:6968 (emit_error_json 'approve' ... 'completion_files_total_miss' ... exit 2) is reached only when FOUR conditions hold, three of them unstated on this surface: (a) `COMPLETION_XCHECK_STATE = checked`, which requires `latest_implementer_completion_record` to return a record -- with no implementer contract the code takes the else-branch at :6903-6907 and sets state 'unestablished', producing an observation and NO refusal; (b) `COMPLETION_XCHECK_MISSING > 0` (:6912), so an empty `files_changed` declaration falls through to the 'PASSED' branch; (c) `COMPLETION_XCHECK_MATCHED = 0`; and (d) `xtotal_survivor_count > 0` (:6951-6967), i.e. at least one declared-but-missing path SURVIVES the WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX filter -- the code's own comment names the all-denylisted declaration as a deliberate exemption ('a specialist who legitimately declared only denylisted paths produces matched=0 honestly'). So an approval in which NONE of the declared files are in the bound change set does NOT refuse when every declared path is denylisted. Everything else in the section verifies exactly: the PostToolUse matcher is `^(Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit)$` (.claude/hooks/hooks.json:50, .claude/settings.json:63), `completion_files_crosscheck` is a real function (qa-gate.sh:3590) and :15285 states it 'reports, never refuses', the refusal does name four numbered recovery commands, and `it broke six test specs` matches do5o's own title ('breaks 6 L2 specs (>=139 assertions)').
findings.description: Row 1 is false for the all-denylisted case and silent about the no-implementer-record case -- and the no-implementer-record case is precisely the scenario the section's own opening paragraph describes, where work is done outside the tracked tools ('a file you edit in vim, in your IDE, or from a shell script'). A reader takes away 'if my approval would bind nothing, v5.0.0 stops me'; the true statement is 'if an implementer declared at least one non-denylisted file and none of them is in the bound set, v5.0.0 stops me'. DP4 at docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:810 already states the careful version ('v5.0.0 mitigates the input problem at `approve` ... but does not fix it'); the README is the looser one. Not raised to high because the section heading ('refuses the WORST case') and row 2 are honest, and the mainline case the section exists to describe is correctly stated. Fix: one clause on row 1 -- 'refuses, provided an implementer contract declared at least one non-denylisted file' -- or a sentence after the table naming the two carve-outs.

findings.evidence: 'across **three** design-review rounds — two `needs_revision`, one `satisfactory`'. `satisfactory` is not a value the system produces. The enum is enforced at qa-gate.sh:8501-8502 -- "verdict='$verdict' is not in the allowed enum {satisfied, needs_revision}" / 'set .verdict to either "satisfied" or "needs_revision"' -- and documented the same way at :3931, :4185, :4211. The F4 store agrees: target-23z's three DESIGN-REVIEW v1 comments read `verdict=needs_revision` (2026-09-28T16:33:45Z), `verdict=needs_revision` (17:46:02Z), `verdict=satisfied` (18:12:11Z). The COUNT and the SPLIT are exactly right; only the third token is wrong.
findings.description: It is set in backticks beside `needs_revision`, which IS the literal, so the pair reads as two machine tokens and a reader greps the store or the script for `satisfactory` and finds nothing. Trivial to fix and worth fixing precisely because the correct token sits next to it. Fix: `satisfied`.

findings.evidence: The R2-F1 rewrite reads: '`compute_design_alignment` shells out to `design-conform` as LEG 1 only in default mode; `compute_design_coherence` calls it with `mode="rollup"`, which skips LEG 1 entirely'. The nearest antecedent of 'it' is `design-conform`, and 'compute_design_coherence calls design-conform with mode=rollup' is precisely the proposition R2-F1 disproved. The intended antecedent is `compute_design_alignment` (the call at qa-gate.sh:15963 is `compute_design_alignment "$mapped_task" "rollup"`), and only a reader who already knows design-conform takes no mode argument -- its usage message at :12879 says it 'takes only <task-id>' -- resolves the pronoun correctly.
findings.description: Every substantive clause of the rewrite verifies (I checked :15182, :15963, the :15119-15144 header text, the :16119 tracker read, and the gating direction: `under_coverage_json = $diff - $roll` at :16194 gates at under_n>0, while the opposite direction is explicitly 'informational, not gated' at :16241 -- so an empty tracker does make the rollup vacuous by its own route, exactly as stated). This is a grammar residue, not a factual error. It earns a finding only because it is the one sentence in this change set that a previous round got factually wrong, and the surviving ambiguity points back at the wrong reading. Fix: replace 'calls it' with 'calls `compute_design_alignment`'.

findings.evidence: README says the qnvo rewrite 'is written and reviewed but **deferred to v5.0.1**'; CHANGELOG.md:81 says '`claude-workflow-plugin-qnvo`, written and preserved, deferred to v5.0.1'. The decision record is do5o, whose title is 'the qnvo primitive replacement deferred out of v5.0.0 — implemented and verified, but breaks 6 L2 specs (>=139 assertions)' and whose body says 'implemented, sound, and DEFERRED OUT OF v5.0.0. No files ship from it. Preserved on branch qnvo/primitive-replacement at 1f4bd81, recoverable with one cherry-pick.' The only comment on qnvo carrying the word review is 'INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF THE FIRST FIX ATTEMPT: BLOCK, 2 CRITICAL + 2 HIGH + 2 MED + 1 LOW (sol-codex)' dated 2026-09-21; `ls docs/reviews/ | grep -i qnvo` returns nothing. An independent verification of the CURRENT implementation does exist, recorded in LESSONS.md:338 ('Verified independently at 1f4bd81 against a control worktree at 91b8e6d'), so 'reviewed' is defensible -- but it is the one word of the three accounts that matches none of them, and it displaces 'preserved', which is the operationally load-bearing part (the branch and commit the work is recoverable from).
findings.description: A reader who checks qnvo's own record after reading 'written and reviewed' finds a BLOCK with two criticals and no review artifact, which reads as a contradiction even though the underlying state is fine. Low because the substantive claims around it are all correct (deferred, six specs, v5.0.1 target). Fix: mirror the CHANGELOG -- 'written and preserved on branch `qnvo/primitive-replacement` at 1f4bd81' -- or say 'implemented and independently verified', which is what do5o and LESSONS.md:338 actually support.
